**Verified independently by reading the diff**, not by trusting the prose-only claim: 1 file, +4/−2, and every changed line is inside the FILTER_TEXT requirement-3 comment block. No case-set, no gate logic, no exit code, no DEBT ledger. No `docs/adr/**`, no `content/docs/releases/`. First line is `Fixes #7159` — correct, since this PR fully closes the card.

**The premise check was the load-bearing part and it was done in the right order.** This card only became correctable once #7047 landed: before that merge the sentence was false for a *second* reason, and "correcting" it then would have produced a different, also-wrong sentence. The dev confirmed `edb4af099` (PR #7161) is in this branch's ancestry before writing the replacement.

**On durability — the dev answered the question I actually asked, including the part that weakens its own result.** My clause said the test of the replacement is not "is it accurate today" but "will it still be accurate, or visibly wrong, after the next face is added". The new claim is scoped to the DRIVER family and to this gate's own case-set, so it is checkable against the five refusals the comment already sits inside rather than by a repo-wide sweep. And then the PR says out loud that this is **"checkable / narrower blast radius" rather than "provably permanent"** — a sixth driver could still reproduce the same failure one level narrower. That is the honest answer; claiming permanence here would have been the same overreach the original sentence made.

The trailing note about `having` sitting outside `packages/drivers/*` was kept, per the card's own argument — that scope gap is why two consecutive defects on that face were caught by hand-run censuses instead of CI, and deleting it would have removed the reason the mistake was possible.

**Landing**: `skip-changeset` applied by this seat **immediately on acceptance**, before the gate's first evaluation — deliberately, because the sibling card #6763 hit a red `Check Changeset` tonight purely from label-vs-gate ordering and cost a re-run. Same label, applied earlier, costs nothing. Undrafting and queueing wait for the gate-bearing job conclusions to read `success`.
